rationale: The cash-to-price leg replicates the already-tested Net-Cash/Short-Debt liquidity legs and the "fixed-charge" denominator (xsga+xint) is really an SG&A-intensity rescaling already captured by Liquid Platform Productivity Value, making this a cosmetic denominator swap within a saturated family rather than a new mechanism.

The first leg is literally identical to Short-Debt Coverage Liquidity Value's liquidity leg and the second is a cash-conversion (inverse-accruals) ratio close to the already-failed Cash-Converted EBITDA Claim Value, with the ABS(oibdp) denominator further scrambling interpretation for loss-making firms.

It is essentially a double sort of two known anomalies (earnings yield and cash holdings), but it usefully inverts the archive's structure by putting profitability in the valuation leg and cash as the conditioner, which is a legitimate diagnostic of where the liquidity family's power originates.

The liquidity leg is byte-for-byte the Net Current Liquidity Surplus leg and the profitability leg is the RnD-Hurdle Liquidity Value numerator with only the scaling denominator changed from at to xsga+xrd, so this is a recombination of two archived signals rather than a new hypothesis.

This is a near-duplicate of Cash-Runway Glamour Burn (same NEG after-interest profitability leg plus xrd, valuation denominator che+dlc swapped for sale+che) and of Intangible Platform Glamour Fade, offering no mechanism beyond the already-documented expensive-and-unprofitable short.

Expensive-assets × weak-post-depreciation-profitability is the standard value×profitability interaction (already probed by Glamour Profit Fade), and adding che to at in the denominator double-counts cash that is already inside total assets, so the valuation leg's economic meaning is muddled.
